html:
King of the Duala people of Douala, educated in Germany, who led the protest against a German plan to expel the Duala from their riverside land, and was hanged for treason on 8 August 1914.

The Germans of Kamerun wanted the land for a white town. Manga Bell petitioned the German parliament and sought allies among other kings, including the Bamum, which the Germans called a plot. He was hanged days after the First World War began, with his secretary Ngoso Din. He is a national hero, and his story is told as an early sign of the fight for Cameroon. See also Ibrahim Njoya.
